## Finite admission and generic named-theory coverage

7 October 2026. [The finite-admission and coverage study](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/ROOT-MATHEMATICAL-COVERAGE-INTEGRATION.md) advances the requested admission and coverage obligations with **36 newly checked Lean theorems and 66 declaration audits**.

On a supplied finite carrier, one target-independent selection construction represents every predicate. Admission of the empty predicate and singletons, with binary-union closure, suffices for full admission. The full predicate carrier and full functions between finite carriers are themselves finite, so the result extends recursively through every finite type in the declared grammar over a finite base, including its graph/ideal presentation. This removes an infinitary closure premise at those scopes; it does not derive the finite base or formation commitments without assumptions.

The higher-order reconstruction now handles arbitrary typed named signatures. Concrete symbol correspondence implies term/formula/sentence truth transport, semantic comprehension and preservation of any theory in that language. Backward interpretation also gives equivalence of satisfiability and semantic consequence over the declared same-universe model classes. The named natural-number addition example is checked; its base and arithmetic remain supplied. A symbol-mismatch example changes truth and shows why the correspondence premise matters, without refuting the fuller root.

**Remaining universal scope:** independently justify infinite bases and their full predicate/function ranges, and establish faithful coverage beyond the declared finite simple-type grammar and supplied semantic resources. Generic named-symbol transport closes the previous representational omission but is not foundation-wide grounding. No independent-agent review or new primary-source retrieval is claimed in this round.
